newsitem.title: USA: NABL meets Feb 27 with SEC's Hunt after criticism.
newsitem.headline: NABL meets Feb 27 with SEC's Hunt after criticism.

text.p: Bond lawyers are set to meet on February 27 with SEC panelist Isaac Hunt to discuss his recent challenge to lawyers to show more leadership on political contributions and other front-burner regulatory issues affecting munis, a spokesperson for lawyers said on Monday.
"We want to respond to his concerns in person," Amy Dunbar, director of governmental affairs for the National Association of Bond Lawyers, said in a telephone interview.
Dunbar said she had no comment on what NABL officials will tell Hunt at the upcoming meeting.
An aide to Hunt was unavailable for comment.

Hunt, who joined the Securities and Exchange Commmission a year ago, told the Bond Club of Virginia on January 22 that he is "troubled" that NABL has not taken aggressive steps to curb "pay-to-play" by member lawyers.
Pay-to-play refers to bond professionals that allegedly give political contributions to elected municipal clients in return for bond business.
Hunt also said bond lawyers are failing to tell clients up front in "retainer" agreements whether they will help protect them from securities law violations.

He cited stinging remarks by U.S. District Judge William Young during a sentencing hearing in December for muni bond dealer Mark Ferber, who was convicted on graft and kickback charges involving bond sales.
"I am simply appalled at the level of practice of the municipal bond lawyers that I have heard about in this case," Hunt said, quoting Young.
